rated_messages.input_message: Instead of smoking, think of 3 things from today that you are grateful for. These can be anything, even small things! Now ask yourself, why are you grateful for these things?
Some places trigger powerful cravings, that is to be expected. Stop and notice where in your body you feel those cravings and remind yourself that cravings typically pass in 1 to 3 minutes
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"

Did you know that just seeing other people smoke activates a part of your brain that is connected with the action of you smoking? This can bring on strong urges to smoke. One simple solution is to avoid seeing others smoke.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.

Pause. Notice the feelings you are having without judgement. Let them come and go. Being aware of your feelings means you can make a new choice about how you respond to your urges instead of smoking on autopilot.

The best way to deal with any urges from being around smokers is to get out of the situation briefly until it goes. Make an excuse, go to the toilet, go get some water, pretend you need to get some phone reception!
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.
